court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: 7th Family Court, Mumbai in Petition No. A-1301 of 2006
case_name: 400 053 vs Mrs Bhavna W/O Rajesh Sainani Hindu

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Mr Rajesh s/o Pratap Sainani Hindu, husband
parties.respondent_defendant: Mrs Bhavna W/o Rajesh Sainani Hindu, wife

facts_of_case: Petitioner-husband filed petition for decree of restitution of conjugal rights. Respondent-wife made complaint under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code. Both parties filed application for divorce by mutual consent. Settlement was agreed, including wife withdrawing criminal complaint and waiving future maintenance claims.

legal_principles.principle: A petition presented under Section 13B (1) of the Act cannot be withdrawn by one party unilaterally.
legal_principles.held: Of course, if the Court is satisfied that a consent was not a free consent and it was the result of force, fraud or undue influence then it is a different matter because in such a case the Court is empowered specifically to refuse to grant the decree.
cited_cases: Nachhattar Singh v Harcharan Kaur, A.I.R. 1996 P and H, 201
Smt Chander Kanta vs. Hanskumar and Anr (I) 1998 D.N.C. 509

legal_principles.principle: If one party is allowed to withdraw the consent, even when other grounds, namely that the parties continued to live separately and have not been able to live together, still subsists and reconciliation is not possible then it will frustrate the very purpose of the enactment.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it is clear that it is settled law
cited_cases: Nachhattar Singh v Harcharan Kaur, A.I.R. 1996 P and H, 201
Smt Chander Kanta vs. Hanskumar and Anr (I) 1998 D.N.C. 509

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce by mutual consent
advising on withdrawal of consent in a divorce case
understanding the Hindu Marriage Act and its application
